transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What has brought you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I keep getting stuck checking things. Like locks, work files, notes… even dressing supplies. I lose a lot of time because I don’t feel like I can move on until I’ve done the same routine enough times to calm down.
Right before you start checking things, what kinds of thoughts or fears are going through your mind, if any?

It’s usually this thought that I missed something small. Like, even if I know I cleaned the wound area, or I already checked a CAD file, my mind goes, what if there’s one tiny thing I didn’t catch? Then it turns into… like, what if that causes an infection, or some design mistake that hurts someone. I try to tell myself I checked, but it doesn’t really go away.

When you’re doing these checking routines, do you feel deep down that the amount of checking you’re doing is excessive or doesn’t really make sense, or does it mostly feel reasonable and necessary to you?

I mean… part of me knows it’s too much. Losing hours checking locks or file dimensions or dressing supplies doesn’t really make sense. But in the moment it feels like I’m not allowed to stop until I’ve gone through it enough times and the anxiety comes down.
Do these checking routines always come after a specific, unwanted thought or image popping into your mind, or do you more often just feel a general worry or tension that makes you check things a lot?

It’s usually more like a specific thought cutting in, I guess. Like I’ll know I cleaned something or checked a CAD file, but then it’s, “What if I missed one tiny thing?” And then my mind jumps to infection or a mistake hurting someone. I can’t really reason it away.
Over a typical week, about how much time per day do you spend caught up in these checking routines, from when they start until you’re finally able to move on?

It depends on the day, but… usually it adds up to a couple hours. Sometimes more if I get stuck with locks or the file checks. It’s not constant all day, but once I start, I can lose a lot of time before I feel like I’m allowed to move on.
Because of these checking routines and the anxiety around them, have you actually been missing deadlines, making mistakes at work, or having problems in your relationships or daily responsibilities?

Yeah… some. Work is probably the main one. My project deadlines have started slipping because I stay late rechecking things until I feel okay enough to submit them.

And outside work, I’ve stopped making it to paddleboarding meetups or workouts sometimes. The routines just… eat up the time I used to keep for myself.

Outside of those moments when a specific “what if I missed something and someone gets hurt” thought suddenly pops in, do you also spend a lot of your day feeling generally worried or tense about many different things, even when you’re not checking anything?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think it’s… all day about everything. It’s more when something sets it off. Otherwise I can feel a bit on edge, but I haven’t really tracked it.

On days when nothing in particular has triggered your checking, do you still find yourself worrying a lot about different things like health, money, work, or family for much of the day, or are you mostly okay until a specific checking-type thought pops up?

I think I’m mostly okay until something specific pops up. I mean, I can be a little tense sometimes, but I don’t usually sit there worrying about money or health or family all day… at least I haven’t noticed that. It’s more when a checking thought starts.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling noticeably more down or unable to enjoy things most of the day, nearly every day?

I… don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been stressed and kind of worn out, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been down most of the day nearly every day. Enjoying things is harder when I’m tired, I guess, but… I’m not sure it’s like that.
